title: The End of the Non-Proliferation Paradigm
author: Jennifer Kavanagh
content:
![The End of the Non-Proliferation
Paradigm](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/07/AP25010356914182.jpg)

Although President Trump is often unpredictable, he has been consistent on one
issue throughout his presidency: Iran will never be allowed to acquire a
nuclear weapon. During the 2016 presidential campaign, Trump lambasted the
2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA)[ _as a
"terrible"_](https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/worldviews/wp/2016/04/03/donald-
trump-repeats-stereotype-about-iranians-when-attacking-
obama/?ref=compactmag.com) deal that gave Iran too much sanctions relief and
protected its enrichment capacity. Once in office, he withdrew the United
States from the agreement. Since then, Trump has used a combination of
increasingly severe economic pressure, aggressive diplomacy, and military
force to try to coerce Iran into ending its nuclear program altogether,
culminating in Operation Epic Fury, a campaign of air, sea, and ground strikes
carried out alongside Israel. The issue featured prominently in recent
negotiations between Vice President JD Vance and Iranian leaders, and remains
at the top of Trump's list of objectives as[ _hostilities
resumed_](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/07/19/world/iran-war-strikes-
trump-hormuz/heres-the-latest?smid=url-share&ref=compactmag.com) over the
weekend.

With the ceasefire over and fighting ongoing, a final resolution of the war
remains elusive. But Trump's primary objective--permanently shutting the door
on Iran's nuclear program--is likely to be out of reach regardless. Instead,
Trump's war is more likely to have exactly the opposite effect: convincing
Tehran that pursuing a nuclear weapon is the only real path to security.
Worse, other states, including US allies and adversaries, may come to the same
conclusion. In the end, a war aimed at preventing proliferation seems likely
to accelerate it. The United States should acknowledge this emerging reality
and start working now to shape it to its own benefit.
